transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-21 10:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (AtlasPay CTO), Laura Gomez (AtlasPay DevOps), Mike Chen (AtlasPay Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): weekly check-in for private VPC pilot, addressed a routing issue causing intermittent 5xxs, reviewed perf numbers after microcode/kernel patch, agreed on next steps to run additional perf sweeps and share security artifacts.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Hayes: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we got a full agenda but let's start with a quick check-in. Priya and I will go over the latest infra fixes and perf numbers. Samir, Laura, Mike, how's your side?
[00:24] Samir Patel: Hey Jordan, yeah thanks. We pushed the NAT gateway route tweak yesterday per Priya's notes, saw fewer connection resets but still occasional spikes in tail latency.
[00:38] Priya Nair: Right, the route table change fixed most of the asymmetric routing we were seeing. There's still one path where the firewall is silently dropping TCP keepalives, we're asking security team to surface logs.
[00:55] Mike Chen: sorry, that was me, I was digging, the flow logs show some drops for the 10.2.0.0/16 prefix to the inference nodes - looks like a policy mismatch with our transit gateway. will share a snippet.
[01:20] Jordan Hayes: Great, appreciate that. On the Redwood side we rolled a microcode/kernel selection update to the runtime on Tuesday - changed the kernel selector to prefer bfloat-friendly kernels for the open model, that reduced per-token CPU time.
[01:40] Laura Gomez: quick question, when you say kernel selector, is that the automatic selection you talked about in the docs? we saw a file named kernel-config.yaml but not sure which field toggles it.
[01:53] Priya Nair: yes, it's automatic but we also expose a flag. it's kernel_preference: performance|compat, default is performance. we'll send the exact field in the notes.
[02:10] Samir Patel: ok thanks. we ran two baseline tests after the patch: median latency down ~8%, p95 down ~12% but p99 still has 2x spikes intermittently.
[02:28] Priya Nair: Those p99s usually correlate with cold KV cache misses or when batching tries to coalesce long sequences. are you seeing sequence length variance in the logs?
[02:40] Laura Gomez: yes, we have a mix - some jobs with 128 tokens, some longer 800 tokens. the long ones blow past the batching window.
[02:53] Jordan Hayes: we recommend prefix caching for repeated prompts and setting a sequence length cap or a separate route for long form. also the quantization profile affects long-seq perf - Q4_0 gave you better throughput in our tests but sometimes worsened tail latency on very long sequences.
[03:18] Mike Chen: on the security side, we need SOC2 Type II evidence and KMS integration docs. do you have HSM options? our compliance team insists.
[03:33] Priya Nair: yes we support customer-managed KMS and HSM via the private deployment; we'll attach the KMS integration guide. SOC2 artifacts we can share under the NDA folder, Jordan will follow up.
[03:49] Jordan Hayes: noted, I'll send the compliance package.
[04:00] [brief pause, crosstalk]
[04:12] Priya Nair: back to networking - Laura, can you confirm whether your VPC peering is active for the inference subnet? sometimes AWS will mark the peering as active but route tables aren't updated.
[04:28] Laura Gomez: it's active, routes are added but we've seen traffic egress through the nat-gw to another AZ intermittently.
[04:40] Samir Patel: that was the asymmetric routing we mentioned, one of our transit gateways has a stale route to a legacy subnet.
[04:52] Priya Nair: ok so immediate remediation is to remove that stale route or add a more specific route with higher priority. we'll share exact route table snapshot format you should grep for.
[05:10] Jordan Hayes: quick perf numbers from Redwood test runs on Tuesday: -- throughput baseline for your model family at sequence 128, batch 8: 420 tokens/sec median; with Q4_0 quantization that rose to ~610 tokens/sec, latency median 70ms->50ms. p99s went 340ms->310ms, so improvement but tail still elevated.
[05:42] Laura Gomez: that's promising on median but we care about the tail since our user SLAs are strict. any mitigation strategies?
[05:55] Priya Nair: a few levers: 1) separate long-seq traffic onto a dedicated route and smaller batch sizes, 2) enable prefix/KV caching for repeated context, 3) reduce coalescing window to lower burst latency, 4) consider a small dedicated GPU pool for predictable tails.
[06:20] Samir Patel: cost tradeoffs? dedicated GPUs are expensive.
[06:27] Jordan Hayes: yes, that's where Redwood Dedicated or reserved nodes come in; for POC we can recommend a tiny dedicated pool 1-2 cards to stabilize tail while keeping rest on shared capacity. we'll model cost impact.
[06:40] Mike Chen: another question: are you doing TLS termination in our VPC or at Redwood side? we want no plaintext outside.
[06:50] Priya Nair: TLS terminates at the customer ingress in the private deploy; we support mTLS between the control plane and nodes with customer certs. we'll send the cert rotation doc.
[07:04] [00:07:10 timestamping drift in auto gen]
[07:15] Laura Gomez: we hit a 502 yesterday around 03:12 UTC, logs show a failure during the auto-update process - was there an upgrade pushed?
[07:28] Jordan Hayes: we pushed a minor runtime patch to address a memory leak in the KV cache last night; the update should be rolling but we do have an automatic failback. looks like your node didn't fully restart before traffic resumed.
[07:45] Priya Nair: yes that explains the 502 - the health checks may not have been marked green before the LB forwarded traffic. for the on-prem package we have an orchestration hook to drain and verify. I'll send the runbook.
[08:02] Samir Patel: can we disable auto-updates during the POC? we prefer manual control until we stabilize.
[08:11] Jordan Hayes: absolutely, we can set updates to manual for your pilot cluster. good call.
[08:20] Priya Nair: action: I'll flip auto-updates to manual and confirm in Slack.
[08:28] Mike Chen: on audit logs, can you provide structured request logs with redaction rules? we need to prove no PII is stored.
[08:39] Jordan Hayes: yes, we have token-level redaction and can provide configurable retention. we'll include a sample redacted log in the docs.
[08:50] [short silence]
[08:58] Priya Nair: ok moving to perf tuning results: we did three test runs yesterday; the public test harness you ran earlier produced similar median numbers but a different p99 profile - I think that's due to your NAT gateway churn.
[09:15] Laura Gomez: how do we prove NAT is the cause?
[09:20] Priya Nair: correlate VPC flow logs with request traces; look for retransmits and TCP handshake delays. we saw grouping of retried connections in the same minute windows as p99 spikes.
[09:33] Samir Patel: we'll pull the flows and send them over.
[09:36] Jordan Hayes: also, for the builtin caching we recommend setting cache key granularity to session-level rather than full prompt for your use case - avoids cache misses when prompts have small metadata diffs.
[09:50] Mike Chen: from compliance, we need proof of encryption at rest for checkpoints and model artifacts. is that supported for private?
[09:58] Priya Nair: yes, everything at rest is encrypted using customer-managed KMS in the private deployment; HSM options are available for customers that require FIPS-level keys. we'll attach the encryption matrix.
[10:12] Laura Gomez: thanks. regarding the on-prem upgrade you mentioned earlier, what's the downtime model? we can't afford long windows.
[10:22] Jordan Hayes: the on-prem package supports rolling upgrades with node draining; typical downtime is minimal for new runtime patches - most of the time it's just the time to restart a node's runtime which is roughly 90-120s per node, assuming no heavy GC. we'll share the step-by-step.
[10:40] Priya Nair: side note: if you want zero user-impact, you can run a small canary pool and route a small percent of traffic for validation before full cutover.
[10:52] Samir Patel: can you model that in the next cost estimate?
[10:58] Jordan Hayes: yes, we'll include canary cost and time-to-stability in the estimate.
[11:05] [11:05 - 18:00 minutes of more detailed debugging and log snippets exchanged; paraphrased below due to time]
[11:06] Priya Nair: shared the exact grep and flow log example in chat - look for RST or Retransmit counts and correlate with request ids. Also, we captured a kernel selection traceback that shows the runtime switching kernels mid-inference on long sequences - that's rare but can spike p99. We'll propose a patch to prefer a single kernel path for long sequences.
[11:30] Laura Gomez: ok we will run the profile tests with a static kernel preference and share results.
[12:00] Mike Chen: security will sign off once we see the HSM/KMS integration doc and the redacted audit logs. we expect those by EOW.
[12:12] Jordan Hayes: noted. Priya will send the docs and patch notes. also we'll turn off auto-updates for your cluster until you give the green light.
[12:25] Priya Nair: action recap: send networking diag, kernel toggle fields, patch notes for KV cache fix, KMS/HSM integration doc, and sample redacted logs. Will do by Friday 2025-05-23.
[12:40] Samir Patel: AtlasPay action recap: provide VPC flow logs and firewall rules, run perf tests (batch 8 and 16), validate route table and remove stale routes; send results by 2025-05-27.
[13:00] Jordan Hayes: ok let's schedule a deeper ops session next week to walk infra folks through route tables and NAT configs. who should be on that invite?
[13:12] Laura Gomez: me and Samir, maybe our network lead (I'll add them). Mike will join for the compliance piece.
[13:20] Jordan Hayes: great. I'll propose two time slots end of next week.
[13:30] [meeting wrap]
[13:35] Jordan Hayes: thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and the modeling. any last questions?
[13:40] Samir Patel: nothing further, thanks.
[13:42] Jordan Hayes: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
